guards.literal_old:
In Part~4.2, every irreducible singular
support whose normalization has a
resolution birationally ruled over a
curve of genus at least two has
nonnegative Euler number. The
normalization may be singular.
guards.literal_new:
Let $f:Y\to B$ satisfy the torus-fibration hypotheses of
\cref{night:P4.12}, and let $mS$ be a fibre with irreducible,
reduced, singular support. Let $\nu:N\to S$ be the normalization
and $\pi:T\to N$ its minimal resolution. Suppose that $T$ is
birationally ruled over a curve of genus at least two. Then
$e(S)\ge0$, including when $N$ is singular.
guards.reason: Resolve the standing-domain locator and name the normalization and minimal resolution.
guards.mathematical_transport: Part 4.2 is the exact torus-fibration domain now stated in night:P4.12. The maps are ν:N→S and π:T→N; a resolution and its minimal resolution have the same birational ruled model. The original permission for singular N remains explicit.
The two proof items keep their order; the iteration prefix is removed.

guards.literal_old:
\item Use the minimal resolution and effective
integral divisor of P4R.6. Push this
divisor to the minimal ruled model
$T_0$. Its intersection with a ruling
fibre is two. The adjunction and
Riemann--Hurwitz calculation in P4R.3
therefore gives exactly
\[
 D_0=2H+\sum_j a_jF_j,
 \qquad a_j\in\mathbb Z_{>0},
\]
with $H$ a smooth section. The reverse
blowup coefficient is the integral
number $\mu-1$. At a conductor crossing
one has $\mu\ge2$, so its exceptional
curve remains in the support and
subdivides the edge. At a smooth
conductor point the operation either
adds a rational leaf or leaves the
reduced curve unchanged. Thus
$A=\operatorname{Supp}D$ is connected,
is $H$ with rational trees attached,
and $\pi_1(A)\to\pi_1(T)$ is an
isomorphism.
guards.literal_new:
\item Put $\rho=\nu\circ\pi$, and take the effective integral
divisor $D$ from \cref{night:P4R.6}. Let $\beta:T\to T_0$ be
a sequence of point blowdowns to a minimal ruled surface and
put $D_0=\beta_*D$. The canonical divisor identity makes
$K_T+D$ torsion, so $K_{T_0}+D_0\equiv0$. The intersection
of $D_0$ with a ruling fibre is two. The adjunction and
Riemann--Hurwitz calculation in the proof of
\cref{night:P4R.3} uses these numerical and effectiveness
hypotheses and gives
\[
 D_0=2H+\sum_j a_jF_j,
 \qquad a_j\in\mathbb Z_{>0},
\]
where $H$ is a smooth section and the $F_j$ are distinct
ruling fibres.

At a reverse point blowup, a centre of multiplicity $\mu$
gives exceptional coefficient $\mu-1$. At a crossing,
$\mu\ge2$, so the exceptional curve subdivides the edge of
the reduced divisor. At a smooth point, it adds a rational
leaf when $\mu\ge2$ and leaves the reduced divisor unchanged
when $\mu=1$. Thus $A=D_{\rm red}$ is the strict transform
of $H$ with rational trees attached, and is connected.
Collapsing those trees to their attachment points induces
an isomorphism on fundamental groups by van Kampen.
The ruling and point blowdowns also induce isomorphisms
on fundamental groups. Their composite restricts on the
strict transform of $H$ to the section isomorphism with
the ruling base. Therefore the inclusion
$j:A\hookrightarrow T$ induces an isomorphism
$j_*:\pi_1(A)\to\pi_1(T)$.
guards.reason: Resolve the divisor/ruled-model references and make the fundamental-group inclusion map explicit.
guards.mathematical_transport: ρ=νπ and β:T→T0 are separate specified morphisms. D0=β_*D and K0+D0≡0 give D0·F=2; the same adjunction/Riemann–Hurwitz computation gives 2H+Σa_jF_j. The exact coefficient a=μ−1 preserves all three blowup cases. Collapsing attached rational trees and composing with the ruling proves j_*:π1(D_red)→π1(T) is an isomorphism, without identifying the degree-two homology groups.

guards.literal_old:
\item Put $C=\operatorname{Sing}(S)_{\rm red}$.
The map $\rho$ is proper and is an
isomorphism outside $A$, and P4R.6
identifies $A$ with its full inverse
image of $C$. The continuous map
$T\cup_A C\to S$ is therefore a
compact-to-Hausdorff bijection and a
homeomorphism. The same cofibration
and van Kampen argument as P4R.3 gives
$\pi_1(S)\simeq\pi_1(C)$. This retains
the exceptional components that map
to points, as well as the strict
conductor components that map to
curves. P4R.1 and the normalization
graph calculation in P4R.3 give
$e(C)\ge0$. Finally P4.13 gives
$e(S_{\rm reg})\ge0$, so
$e(S)=e(S_{\rm reg})+e(C)\ge0$.
guards.literal_new:
\item Put $C=\operatorname{Sing}(S)_{\rm red}$.
Proposition~\ref{night:P4R.6} gives $A=\rho^{-1}(C)_{\rm red}$,
and $\rho$ identifies $T\setminus A$ with $S_{\rm reg}$.
In the quotient $T\cup_A C$, every fibre of $\rho$ over
$c\in C$ is identified with $c$. The induced map to $S$
is consequently a continuous bijection from a compact
space to a Hausdorff space, hence a homeomorphism.
This quotient uses the whole proper map $\rho|_A:A\to C$,
including the exceptional components contracted to points.

A triangulation of the analytic pair $(T,A)$ makes
$A\subset T$ a subcomplex and a cofibration
\cite[Theorem~2, p.~464]{Lojasiewicz1964}.
The associated double mapping cylinder has the homotopy
type of this pushout. Van Kampen therefore gives
\[
 \pi_1(S)\simeq
 \pi_1(T)*_{\pi_1(A)}\pi_1(C)\simeq\pi_1(C).
\]
For the second isomorphism, the inverse map is identity
on $\pi_1(C)$ and is $(\rho|_A)_*j_*^{-1}$ on
$\pi_1(T)$; these maps agree on the amalgamating group.
Proposition~\ref{night:P4R.1} makes $\pi_1(C)$ virtually abelian.

Let $c$ be the number of irreducible
components of $C$, let $g_i$ be their normalization genera,
and let $b$ be the cycle rank of its normalization incidence
graph. The calculation in \cref{night:P4R.3} gives
\[
 \pi_1(C)\simeq
   \Bigl(*_i\pi_1(C_i^{\rm norm})\Bigr)*F_b,
 \qquad e(C)=c+1-2\sum_i g_i-b.
\]
Virtual abelianness permits either all $g_i=0$ with
$b\le1$, or one $g_i=1$ with $b=0$. These give respectively
$e(C)=c+(1-b)\ge0$ and $e(C)=c-1\ge0$.
Finally \cref{night:P4.13}, applied to this same fibre $mS$,
gives $e(S_{\rm reg})\ge0$. Additivity yields
\[
 e(S)=e(S_{\rm reg})+e(C)\ge0.
\]
guards.reason: State the proper pushout and its inverse group map, and resolve the curve/Euler references.
guards.mathematical_transport: A=D_red=ρ⁻¹(C)_red identifies the same subset of T. The continuous bijection T∪_A C→S uses every contracted fibre and is a homeomorphism. The cofibration gives the group amalgam; its inverse is identity on π1(C) and (ρ|A)_*j_*⁻¹ on π1(T). The exact normalization graph has Euler c+1−2Σg_i−b, and the virtually abelian cases give the same nonnegative bound. WK applies to the unchanged mS, yielding the same e(S) conclusion.
